result.summary:
Venuvoy describes itself, everywhere, as a sports-trip PLANNER built on trustworthy data, not a booking app: "Venuvoy plans sports trips around real fixtures" (README), "A sports trip you can trust." (hero). You give a country or city, dates and what you love (a form, or one free sentence in Hebrew or English that fills the planner), and it builds 2-3 genuinely different, priced plans ("Big Matches", "Balanced", "Easy Pace") on a map and timeline, each item with a source, check date and status; a paid tracking option then watches the fixtures and alerts with replacements.

The founder is right that it is far wider than football: 16 spectator sports in the wizard (football, basketball, baseball, ice hockey, American football, motorsport, rugby, tennis, golf and more), golf rounds and stadium tours on free days, "active days" the traveller does themselves (hikes, city runs, parkrun), a "Sport nearby" layer of about 16,000 places (courts, climbing, pools, karting, shooting ranges, skydiving, sports museums, club stores) in 520 cities, and an opt-in, adults-only "Nightlife and casinos" option (18 casinos, one per trip, on a free evening, as a place to visit).

Three corrections the ads need. (1) Venuvoy states repeatedly that it "does not sell tickets, flights or hotels": tickets are a "Get tickets" guide to official channels, hotels are a partner search link, flights are only times the user types in; the budget is "Excluding flights and hotels". (2) The sentence fills the planner; the user then presses "Create plans". (3) Casinos carry a hard rule: "Venuvoy does not offer or promote gambling", never for parties with children. Live languages: Hebrew (default) and English; display currencies ILS, USD, EUR, GBP. Concerts and bars are not in the product.

facts.claim: Casinos: an option called "Nightlife and casinos" / "חיי לילה וקזינו" in the wizard's free-days step. Off by default, adults only ("18+ (21+ in some countries, including the US), ID required"), disabled for a party with children. When on, the planner may add at most ONE casino per trip on a free evening (from 19:00), shown only as a place to visit with minimum age, ID, dress code, entry fee, hours, what to see and the official site. No betting content, no partner or affiliate link, never a "Surprise me" pick.

Casino wording the product itself uses, binding for ads: card note "Listed only as a place to visit. Venuvoy does not offer or promote gambling." / "מוצג כמקום לבקר בו בלבד. Venuvoy לא מציעה ולא מקדמת הימורים."; terms: "A casino is listed only as a place to visit: Venuvoy does not offer, arrange or promote gambling of any kind, and every casino is shown with the minimum entry age under local law."

Casino data: 18 casinos in 17 catalog cities (Monaco, Las Vegas x2, London, Venice, Madrid, Barcelona, Paris area, Melbourne, Singapore, Montreal, Spa, Frankfurt area, Mainz/Wiesbaden, Santander, Adelaide, Chicago, Miami area); 10 confirmed, 8 provisional. All 18 are present in the shipped region files. The research note says someone should still open each source page before launch.

"Nightlife" today means casinos only. Sports bars and bar games ("Game at a bar": "Pub that shows sport", "Bar games (billiards, darts)") have labels but are marked release 3, the seed rejects them, and the shipped spots index has 0 "watch" places.

The one-sentence box is real but it FILLS THE PLANNER, it does not output the trip: title "Tell us in one sentence" / "ספרו לנו במשפט אחד", sub "We fill in the planner with what we recognise. Anything we don't stays blank for you to complete.", button "Fill in the planner" / "מלאו לי את האשף"; the user then presses "Create plans" / "ליצור מסלולים". On the landing page the default is a form (destination, dates, sport chips); the sentence sits behind the toggle "Or describe it in one sentence". It reads Hebrew and English with a local grammar (cities, dates, sports, teams, budget, nights, party); an AI model helps only in the full version.

The three example sentences the product suggests. EN: "A week in London mid-November, Manchester for a day, football and golf, ₪7,000"; "Next weekend in Madrid with my son, must see Real Madrid"; "NBA and golf in New York in early December, two of us, $3,000". HE: "שבוע בלונדון באמצע נובמבר, יום במנצ'סטר, כדורגל וגולף, 7,000 ₪"; "סוף השבוע הבא במדריד עם הבן, חובה לראות את ריאל מדריד"; "NBA וגולף בניו יורק בתחילת דצמבר, זוג, 3,000 דולר". README example: "a week in London mid-November, two matches".

The sentence parser does not know the word casino (no match in the parser), and it treats "nightlife", "hotel(s)", "flight(s)", "tickets" as filler words to skip. It does understand hiking and running ("three days of hiking", "שלושה ימי טרק"). So an ad must not show someone typing "…and a casino night" and getting one from the sentence; the casino is a toggle.

facts.claim: Venuvoy does NOT sell or book tickets, flights or hotels. Terms intro: "It does not sell tickets, flights or hotels and is not a party to any purchase you make elsewhere." Footer on every page: "Venuvoy does not sell tickets. All purchases happen with official bodies or linked partners." / "Venuvoy אינה מוכרת כרטיסים. כל הרכישות מתבצעות אצל הגופים הרשמיים או השותפים המקושרים." Pricing FAQ: "Does Venuvoy sell tickets? No. We link to official bodies and partners and the purchase happens there. You pay Venuvoy only for planning and tracking."

What it does for tickets, hotels and flights instead. Tickets: one "Get tickets" action per game with difficulty, steps, deadlines, official links, prices and ballots, plus a ticket link check ("Ticket shield"). Hotels: a partner search link per city you stay in (Booking.com), described as "Optional: the plan never depends on them." Flights: only the traveller's own landing and departure times, used to avoid a match too soon after landing, and a "Land by {time}" chip. The budget field is "Budget for tickets and travel — Excluding flights and hotels." No flight search or flight partner exists in the partner registry (Booking.com, Booking.com Cars, GetYourGuide, Seat Unique, P1 Travel, Ticketmaster, StubHub, SeatGeek).

One user-facing line does mention flights loosely: on a public ticket page, "Plan a trip around this event — flights, where to stay and more matches that week." This is the only place I found the product's own copy implying flights are part of the plan.

The output: 2–3 plan versions on a map and a timeline, named "Big Matches" (המשחקים הגדולים), "Balanced" (מאוזן) and "Easy Pace" (בקצב רגוע), each with a 0–100 score from feasibility, quality and data health; every event has reasons, every left-out event a why-not. What-if editing (lock, swap, remove, add), compare side by side, date shift, budget stress test, dated checklist, venue-day guide (leave-by time, getting there and back, ground rules), share links, print/PDF, calendar file, WhatsApp text, offline companion.

The trust promise ("How we check"): "A source for every row — Every fixture and price comes with a source link and a check date." "A person confirms — Only a human check against the official site marks a row confirmed." "Estimates are marked — Estimated travel, currency and prices always show with ≈." How-it-works header: "Venuvoy does not sell tickets and promises nothing it has not checked." Statuses: Confirmed, Provisional, Subject to change, Unverified.

Tracking: "We watch the events in your plan and alert you on time, venue or cancellation changes, with replacement suggestions. Tracking runs until a day after your last check-out." Up to three feasible replacements per alert; optional autopilot applies small changes automatically with one-tap undo. In demo mode it is a change simulator in the browser; real tracking needs the backend (scheduled functions, email).

Pricing: planning is free ("Planning is free. Pay once per trip to edit, execute and watch it."); not a subscription ("No. One payment per trip."). Plan unlock ₪49 / $15 / €14 / £12; Tracking ₪99 / $29 / €27 / £23; Bundle ₪129 / $39 / €36 / £31. Free: wizard, 2–3 variants, full itinerary, map, costs, provenance, compare, one share link, official ticket links. Refund: full within 14 days if no export or unlock action was taken.

Languages: Hebrew (default, right-to-left, served at "/") and English ("/en") are live. Russian, Arabic, French and Spanish are registered as "planned": the i18n/ar, es, fr, ru folders contain only a .gitkeep, and the loader is a stub ("it installs nothing yet, so every extra-locale string still renders in English"). README names "es, fr, de and ar" as planned, which disagrees with the registry (ru, not de).

Currencies: display currencies are ILS, USD, EUR, GBP; the price book is quoted in the same four, fixed per currency and never converted. Default display currency is ILS in Hebrew and USD in English. Local prices are shown in the original currency first with an approximate conversion; the catalog holds exchange rows for 43 currencies.

Coverage is wide but uneven. 46 destination regions (most of Europe, USA in three parts, Canada, Brazil, Japan, UAE, plus "Marquee events worldwide" in 31 countries). Only England is tier "Full coverage"; the rest are "Partial coverage" or "Marquee events only". The app itself tells users "We do not cover {city} yet". So "for any city" / "לכל עיר בעולם" in the SEO description is the product's own claim but is not literally true of the data.

The six real example trips on the landing page ("Plans the engine actually generated — Not mock-ups: trips the engine ran on the real catalog."): Madrid and Barcelona, a LaLiga double weekend; Manchester derby weekend with Old Trafford and Etihad stadium tours; Milan and Turin, the derby and Juventus; Munich, Champions League night, Bundesliga and an Alps rest day; Las Vegas Formula 1 weekend; Paris, Le Classique and the Six Nations (football plus rugby). Five of six are football-led.

Call-to-action vocabulary is plan / see / create / get / unlock, never book or buy for Venuvoy's own action: "Plan a trip" / "לתכנון טיול"; hero button "See what's on" / "מה יש בתאריכים שלי"; "Fill in the planner"; "Create plans" / "ליצור מסלולים"; "Get tickets · On sale" / "להשיג כרטיסים · במכירה"; "Unlock this trip" / "פתיחת הטיול"; "Build a trip around this match" / "לבנות טיול סביב המשחק"; "+ To my plan". "Bookings around your plan" is the title of the optional partner-links section only. Hero hint: "No account · 2–3 free plans · edit everything later" (demo build) or "Free account · 2–3 plans at no cost" (full build).

facts.claim: Tone of voice rules: "Both languages are written to read naturally on their own (neither reads as a translation of the other), concisely, and without exclamation marks." The name is always "Venuvoy" in Latin letters, in both languages; a Hebrew prefix takes a hyphen ("ב-Venuvoy", "ל-Venuvoy"). In Hebrew the product is feminine ("Venuvoy מתכננת", "Venuvoy לא מוכרת"). Voice is calm, factual and honest about limits ("promises nothing it has not checked", "without polish").

Shabbat and Jewish holidays planning exists but is shown to an Israeli audience only: "No planning, marketing, account or shared screen shows Shabbat wording outside the audience". Relevant if ads run outside Israel.

More disclaimers: "There are no ads in the service" and no sale of personal data; nobody can pay to appear higher; partner links are labelled "Partner link" and never sit above the official channel; a "confirmed" status "does not mean the fixture cannot move"; following clubs from afar "We don't track broadcasters, so we never say where to watch."; ticket status is "not a promise of availability". All legal documents are marked "Draft pending legal review".
Limits the product states: up to 30 days per trip; up to three destinations; the sentence handles up to two cities to stay in; up to 20 people in each group.

public/ holds no manifest, sitemap or robots file: only the spots data, favicon, icons, og-default.png and showcase/trips.json. The manifest is generated from vite.config.ts (name "Venuvoy", categories sports and travel, shortcuts "Plan a trip · תכנון טיול" and "My trips · הטיולים שלי"); sitemap and robots.txt are written at build time (private areas /admin, /account, /alerts, /trips, /checkout, /s/ disallowed).

Whether the public site today runs in full mode (accounts, Stripe payments, real tracking emails, AI assist) or demo mode cannot be told from the repository; the code supports both and labels demo builds. Package version is 0.1.0 and the last commit is dated 2026-11-11.

Football is not named in the positioning.

Venuvoy does not sell tickets; it says so in the hero, footer, pricing FAQ and how-it-works. 'We link to official bodies and partners and the purchase happens there. You pay Venuvoy only for planning and tracking.'

A trip starts three ways, all ending in the wizard at /plan: (1) the home form: country or city, dates, six sport chips (football, golf, basketball, tennis, motorsport, rugby; 'More sports in the wizard'), button 'See what's on' / 'מה יש בתאריכים שלי'; (2) a one-sentence box on the home page and on /plan; (3) 'Build a trip around this match' on public pages.

The one typed sentence does NOT produce a plan by itself. Its button reads 'Fill in the planner' / 'מלאו לי את האשף'; it prefills the wizard ('Anything we don't [recognise] stays blank for you to complete') and the user then presses 'Create plans' / 'ליצור מסלולים'. Sentences work in Hebrew and English; one example is 'NBA and golf in New York in early December, two of us, $3,000'.

The sentence is read by a deterministic local parser. An optional AI model reads harder sentences only in full mode when a server key is configured; whether that is on in production cannot be seen from the repository.

The wizard has two steps: 'Where, when and what', then optional 'Fine-tune'. Inputs: up to 3 destinations, dates and flexibility (± 1 day to ± 1 week), adults, children and their ages, day-trip radius 30-300 minutes, flight details, 16 spectator sports plus Hike and Run, teams and competitions, must-see match, watch or play, 'Surprise me', free-day extras, budget and pace, own items, a lodging pin, clubs followed from afar, Shabbat. Trips are up to 30 days.

A finished plan is 2-3 versions ('Three takes on your trip, with a map, a timeline and what you can change') with three scores (Feasibility, Fit, Data reliability), a reason for each item, a why-not verdict for each event left out, and a source and check date per item. Transport inside the trip is in the plan: legs between cities by train, plane, coach, car, ferry, public transport or on foot, with a typical time, a fare range, the operator and a 'Book' link to the operator's site; estimates are marked ≈. Budget card (Prepare tab): expected cost in four slices, tickets, travel, activities and a buffer, with a stress test (ticket tier, fare type, party size, currency shock) and one-tap levers. result.summary:
Venuvoy's engine is a deterministic planner (pure TypeScript, no model) that turns a trip description into 2–3 genuinely different, priced, day-by-day plans and then keeps them editable and tracked. It is multi-sport by construction, not football-only.

The shipped catalog (src/data/regions, 46 region files plus core) holds 11,711 events in 13 sports, 88 competitions, 705 teams, 786 venues and 528 cities in 56 countries, dated 2026-10-04 to 2027-12-12. Football is half of it (5,834 events, 41 competitions, 40 countries). The rest is real: MLB 2,428, NBA 1,199, NHL 1,206, EuroLeague 310, EuroCup 160, NFL 192, plus motorsport (F1, MotoGP, Formula E, IndyCar, WEC), tennis, golf, rugby, horse racing, athletics, and one event each for cricket and cycling.

Beyond matches, four things are wired to the user:
- **Casinos:** 18 in 17 cities, opt-in under "Nightlife and casinos", adults only, evening only, one per trip, shown as places to visit and never as gambling.
- **Active days:** 174 hikes, city runs and parkruns the traveller does themselves.
- **Sport nearby:** about 15,960 places in 520 cities to play, tour or shop, including shooting ranges and extreme sports; added by hand only.
- **Golf and stadium tours:** rounds, indoor golf and tours as free-day fillers, in England only.

Three limits matter for ad copy. Venuvoy does not sell tickets, flights or hotels. The one-sentence box fills the planner form; it does not produce the plan directly. "Nightlife" today means casinos only; sports bars are planned and have zero rows.

"Live" below means wired in the code and data at repo HEAD a927bc3; I did not run the app or check the deployed site.

facts.claim: The engine is pure, deterministic TypeScript with no AI model: same inputs and seed give identical plans; 'Regenerate' is seed+1. It runs in the browser (optionally a worker), in tests and inside Supabase edge functions.

Engine input is a structured TripInput, not free text: 1-3 base cities with check-in/out (optional private lodging point), party (adults, children, optional ages), interests per sport (weight 0-3, mode watch/play/both, teams, competitions), budget and currency, pace (relaxed/balanced/packed), arrival/departure times, flexible dates, own items, and preferences (day-trip radius, late returns, rest on arrival day, must-have/avoid/locked events, double headers, rest days, jet-lag day, fillers golf/tours/experiences, includeCasinos, active days, surpriseMe, forced travel mode, Shabbat observance, followed clubs, spots, step-free).
facts.evidence: /home/user/venuvoy/src/types/domain.ts:1271-1426; /home/user/venuvoy/src/features/wizard/types.ts:130 (MAX_BASES = 3), 243-248 (radius 30-300 min, default 150; max 30 trip days; max party 20)

facts.claim: The 'one typed sentence' is an intake box that FILLS THE PLANNER FORM, it does not itself produce the plan. It is a deterministic Hebrew+English parser (cities, dates, sports, teams, budget, party, nights, 'we keep Shabbat'); unmatched words are shown, never guessed; the box says an unrecognised sentence is sent to an AI model that only picks out names and numbers. It handles up to two cities to stay in.

Output is 2-3 plans, never padded: 'Big Matches' (המשחקים הגדולים), 'Balanced' (מאוזן), 'Easy Pace' (בקצב רגוע); an edited plan becomes 'Your plan' (התוכנית שלכם). Plans overlapping by Jaccard > 0.6 are retried or dropped, and a note explains when fewer than three genuinely different plans fit.

Each plan carries three scores: Feasibility (0-100, 100 minus penalties: can it be executed), Quality (weighted: interest_match 30, headline_weight 20, travel_burden 20, rest_balance 15, budget_fit 15) and Health (can the data be trusted now: verification 30, freshness 20, move_risk 20, collision_risk 20, ticket_feasibility 10). Every component has bilingual evidence and an optional fix action.

Events are ranked by interest (sport weight x20, +25 followed team, +15 picked competition), importance (event importance x8, club prestige, competition tier, finals), certainty (data status, known kick-off, move risk), minus travel hours and ticket difficulty; the three versions apply different weights (Big Matches favours importance, Easy Pace penalises travel and caps day trips at 60 minutes with early nights).

A plan holds items of kind event, activity, travel, free, rest, note, placeholder; day kinds; a verdict for EVERY event in the window (included, or excluded with a typed reason such as radius, budget, last train, collision, rest day, Shabbat); cost totals min-max in the display currency split into tickets/travel/activities; and typed warnings (unknown kick-off, last train tight, over budget, weather-sensitive and others).

After generation the engine supports what-if edits (lock, unlock, remove, add, swap, set budget, set pace, double headers, travel mode, casinos on/off, active days, add a spot, own items), a compare view of what each plan gives up, replacement suggestions, a date-shift scan (default plus/minus 7 days, up to 30) that really re-plans each window, and 'start from this match' window proposals.

Tracking compares each planned event with the live catalog and raises alerts (cancelled, postponed, moved, kick-off changed, venue changed, collision, travel infeasible) with up to 3 suggestions; an opt-in Autopilot may apply minor changes inside a consent envelope, never critical ones, with undo.

Picking a country instead of a city yields up to 3 route proposals of one or two bases, built from that country's fixtures in the dates and the traveller's interests; a second base must be within 4 hours door to door.

result.summary: Venuvoy is a sports-trip planner (Hebrew-first web app with PWA install) that sells nothing except its own software features. It never sells, brokers or holds tickets, flights, hotels or casino entries: every purchase happens on an official or partner site it links to. Outbound links: the official club/league/organiser ticket page first, then a compare list of 44 ticket sites (official platforms, fan-to-fan, resale, comparison) with legal warnings; Booking.com hotel searches per stay city; Booking.com Cars; GetYourGuide tours; Seat Unique and P1 Travel hospitality; Ticketmaster, StubHub, SeatGeek in the US. Some links may pay commission through a first-party redirect ("go"); order never depends on commission. Flights are not searched, priced or linked: the planner only asks landing and departure times, and the budget is "for tickets and travel, excluding flights and hotels". Casinos are an opt-in, adults-only evening stop shown with practical facts, with no gambling content and no partner link. Venuvoy's own checkout (Stripe) is one-time per trip: Plan unlock 49 ILS / 15 USD / 14 EUR / 12 GBP, Tracking 99 / 29 / 27 / 23, Bundle 129 / 39 / 36 / 31. Planning is free; it is not a subscription. AI: "assist" (Anthropic Claude) only turns the typed sentence into names and numbers when the local parser fails; planning and "evaluate-plans" (change tracking, alerts, autopilot) are deterministic code, not AI. Live data: ECB exchange rates via frankfurter.app, football fixtures from football-data.org (provisional only), optional ticket prices from sellers' documented APIs (off until keys and written permission). Scam Shield checks a pasted ticket link against official domains; /trust is a public data-status ledger. Honest verbs: plan, find, compare, check, track/alert. Not honest: book, buy, sell, "gets you tickets", "AI plans your trip". Whether Stripe, affiliate ids, price feeds and the AI key are switched on in production cannot be seen from the repository.

(a) Named partners and kinds of sites Venuvoy links to: Booking.com (hotels), Booking.com Cars (car hire, only when the plan has a day trip by road), GetYourGuide (stadium tours and experiences), Seat Unique (UK hospitality: football, rugby, cricket, tennis, horse racing, boxing, darts), P1 Travel (motorsport hospitality), Ticketmaster (official primary tickets, US), StubHub and SeatGeek (resale, US only). (a) How Venuvoy earns: "Venuvoy earns money in two ways: a one-time payment per trip for the paid features, and commissions from some partners when you book through a partner link. (a) Commission plumbing: in full mode a commission-bearing link goes through the first-party `go` edge function, which validates the partner host, applies Venuvoy's affiliate id, records a click row (partner, category, trip id, host; no IP, no user agent, no URL) and redirects. It only earns if affiliate ids (`VITE_PARTNER_*`) are configured; without them every link is plain and earns nothing. Reported commission rates in the code are unverified admin notes.

(b) Venuvoy's own checkout charges for three one-time, per-trip products through Stripe Checkout. Price book in code: Plan unlock 49 ILS / 15 USD / 14 EUR / 12 GBP; Tracking 99 ILS / 29 USD / 27 EUR / 23 GBP; Bundle 129 ILS / 39 USD / 36 EUR / 31 GBP. Prices are fixed per currency, never FX-converted. Stripe line item name is "Venuvoy — Plan unlock / Trip tracking / ...".

Pay once per trip to edit, execute and watch it." / "התכנון חינם. משלמים פעם אחת לטיול כדי לערוך, לבצע ולעקוב." Unlocking happens from inside a trip: "Nothing to buy up front."

(b) What is free: the wizard, 2-3 plan variants, full itinerary with map and timeline, costs and ranges, provenance, plan score, compare view, why-not explorer, scam check, official ticket links with the site comparison, public pages, one share link. No time limit.

(b) Plan unlock adds: what-if editing (lock, swap, remove) and re-plan; ticket playbooks with steps, deadlines and price tiers; dated checklist; exports (calendar ICS, print-PDF, WhatsApp); venue-day guides; budget stress test; offline companion. Tracking adds: change alerts by email and in-app with replacement suggestions, live plan score, companion "what changed", offline companion, until a day after the last check-out. Bundle = both, cheaper than buying separately.

(b) Refunds as written: full refund within 14 days if no export or unlock action was taken; tracking refunded pro-rata before the trip starts; one purchase covers one trip. All legal documents (terms, privacy, refunds, tickets, earnings) are flagged `draft: true`, "bilingual drafts, pending legal review".

(b) Whether real money is charged depends on server secrets not visible in the repo. Without a Stripe key a hosted project answers `503 payments_not_configured` and sells nothing; with `PAYMENTS_DEMO=true` it hands out free demo unlocks and the app says "Stripe is not connected yet, so this trip was unlocked as a demo order. Nothing was charged." Demo mode (no account) records a demo order with no payment.

(c) `assist` is the only AI call. It sends the one typed sentence (max 500 characters) to Anthropic's Claude (`ASSIST_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"`) only when the local deterministic parser could not place a word. It extracts names and numbers only: cities, date phrases, sports, teams, budget, nights, party size. "It never computes calendar dates, never returns a slug, a fixture or a price." The intake "works completely without it"; it is off unless ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set, and capped at 500 calls a day by default.

(c) `evaluate-plans` is NOT AI. It is a scheduled job (every 15 minutes) that re-runs the deterministic planning engine (`evaluatePlan`) on saved plans when a fixture's date, time, venue, status or tickets change, writes alerts with up to three replacements and a fresh plan-health score, and, when the traveller opted in and tracking is paid, applies small changes automatically (autopilot) with one-tap Undo. `notify` then emails alerts via Resend every 20 minutes. No model call exists in the function.

It writes rows as `provisional`; "nothing is upgraded to confirmed by a machine". Everything else in the catalog comes from Venuvoy's own manual research files and openfootball (CC0). Other providers listed in the database (TheSportsDB, Ticketmaster Discovery) have no fixture adapter.

(d) Live ticket prices ("From $84 · checked 3 h ago" on a compare row, and prices per stand on the seat-map page) come only from sellers' documented APIs with Venuvoy's own key, never scraped: Ticketmaster Discovery (face value), SeatGeek (US resale), StubHub International, viagogo. The function is off until its secrets are set; SeatGeek, StubHub International and Ticketmaster Top Picks also need a dated written permission to display; viagogo is switched off in code (`ENABLED = false`). With no key "the list shows no price at all". In demo mode there are none.

(d) Ticket status and prices shown are information with a check date, not availability: public ticket page description "Difficulty, official channels, prices and deadlines for {event} — verified sources, no inventory promises." Legal: "We hold no inventory, set no prices and do not see the transaction. An 'on sale' or 'opens on' status is information from the source on the check date, not a promise of availability."

(e) Scam check = "Scam Shield" / "מגן הכרטיסים", a free public tool at /tools/scam-check (footer label "Ticket shield"). You paste a ticket link or a seller name; it answers one of five verdicts: Official, Authorised, Legal secondary market, Unknown — could not verify, Warning — lookalike. It compares the domain with an allowlist of official bodies and the ticket-site registry and flags look-alike domains, swapped letters, punycode, URL shorteners, free hosts and http. It also shows the country's resale rule, a five-point "Before you pay" checklist and what to do if something goes wrong. It runs in the browser from the engine; no server function is involved.

(e) The scam check is deliberately conservative and is not a guarantee: "Unknown is not a warning: we simply have no record of this seller." Legal: "'Could not verify' is not an accusation, and 'official' is not a guarantee." Only the organiser's own domain reads "Safe to proceed".

(e) The trust page (/trust, titled "Data status" / "מצב הנתונים") is a public verification ledger: per region, how many fixtures are confirmed, provisional or unverified, when they were last checked, from which sources; a coverage map; the list of data providers; where places data comes from (OpenStreetMap, Wikidata, clubs' own sites) with a downloadable database; and a public feed of fixture changes. /how-it-works explains the four statuses, the plan score, the estimates policy and what tracking does: "Venuvoy does not sell tickets and promises nothing it has not checked."

Seat map: "Choose seats on the map" then "Pick an area and we'll compare the ticket sites for it". The map is schematic; "You choose the actual seats on the site you buy from." Badges "Most reliable" and "Cheapest" follow fixed rules that commission never changes.

(f) Verb check against the product's own wording. PLAN: honest ("A sports-trip planner", "Plan a trip", 2-3 priced plans, free). FIND / SEE WHAT'S ON: honest (hero button "See what's on" / "מה יש בתאריכים שלי"). COMPARE: honest (compare plans side by side; "Compare ticket sites"). CHECK: honest (Scam Shield "Check"; every fixture has "a source, a check date and a status"). TRACK / WATCH / ALERT: honest for the paid Tracking product. BOOK and BUY: not honest for Venuvoy itself; the product uses them only for what happens on other sites ("when you book through a partner link", "the purchase happens there"). "Get tickets" is the product's own button label but it opens the official seller; it never promises a ticket.

No sentence saying Venuvoy is "not affiliated with" clubs, leagues or organisers was found in user-facing text. The nearest statements are "is not a party to any purchase you make elsewhere", "we cannot vouch for any third party" and "We never copy texts, images or crests."

result.summary:
Venuvoy's brand is a deliberate, named design direction called "Members' Club" ("מועדון החברים", which the proposal page says the founder chose). It is the opposite of a bright sports-app look: racing-green header band and buttons, cream "fixture-book" paper, ivory cards with a double hairline rule, brass/gold ornaments, oxblood for alerts, near-square corners (1-4px), serif display type. Dark mode is "dark green leather, gilt lettering". It is live on the main branch (globals.css, AppShell, Monogram, favicon.svg) and matches the real-build screenshots in the second design page.

Name: always "Venuvoy" in Latin letters, in Hebrew too. As a logo it is set in Playfair Display, medium weight, UPPERCASE with wide tracking (VENUVOY), cream on green, beside a round crest: a serif "V" in a double brass ring. In running text it is "Venuvoy".

Fonts: Playfair Display (Latin display and wordmark), Frank Ruhl Libre (Hebrew display), Assistant (all body text, both languages). Icons are Lucide thin-outline; small brass diamonds replace sport emoji.

Voice: calm, factual, trust-first. Live hero: "A sports trip you can trust." / "טיול ספורט שאפשר לסמוך עליו." Tagline: "Sports trips built around real fixtures" / "טיולי ספורט סביב משחקים אמיתיים". The product says of itself "Venuvoy does not sell tickets". The product is framed as sports trips, not football only: 16 spectator sports, hikes and runs, golf rounds, stadium tours, sports experiences, and opt-in adult "Nightlife and casinos".

Two cautions for the ads. (1) The installed-app PNG icons and the social share image are still an older identity (navy #0f172a with a mint #34d399 crosshair); do not draw that as the logo. (2) Neither design page contains a brand slogan or audience description; they are layout documents. Slogans come from the product copy.

result.summary:
Venuvoy's own history shows it was never football-only. The repository starts on 2026-10-10 as "Fixtura" (a fixtures-based sports-trip planner, Hebrew-first), is renamed Venuvoy on 2026-10-11, and by the end of day two already carries a USA region, a "marquee" world-events region, golf rounds and stadium tours as activities, and casinos as an opt-in evening attraction. Its own one-line purpose, in README, page meta and landing hero, is "Venuvoy plans sports trips around real fixtures" / "טיולי ספורט סביב משחקים אמיתיים": 2-3 priced alternative plans, every row with source and check date, then tracking of fixture changes. It states twice that it does not sell tickets.

Growth came in waves: 18 Oct "Wave 1" (22 regions: motorsport calendars, EuroLeague, NFL/NBA/NHL, Rugby World Cup, UAE golf/tennis/horse racing); 24-26 Oct "Wave 2" (EuroLeague+EuroCup, UEFA cups, MLB, 12 more domestic leagues, Japan, Scandinavia) plus "Active days" (hikes, city runs, parkrun the traveller does themselves); 1 Nov "Compare ticket sites" (44 sites) and seat maps; 2-8 Nov "Own items" (your own plans in the trip) and "Sport nearby" spots (courts, padel, pools, karting, climbing, shooting ranges, extreme sports, stadium tours, museums, club stores) in 520 cities. Today's catalog: 46 regions, 56 countries, about 11,700 events in 13 sports; football is half of them.

Current work (8-11 Nov): groundwork for four more languages (ru, ar, fr, es; not built yet), showcase date fixes, weekly link repairs. Planned, not shipped: sports bars (release 3), rides/ski/via ferrata (release 2). Deploy configs exist for Netlify and Vercel with default domain venuvoy.app, but the repo holds no proof the site is publicly live; legal pages are "drafts pending legal review".

result.summary:
The founder's own product-defining words in the build chat (10 Oct to 13 Nov) could not be reached. The events API returns 100 raw events per call, which is 3 to 10 minutes of a 36-day session, and almost every event is workflow progress noise. I read the last compaction summary, the session's two design artifacts, the founder's last messages there, and the ads chat's local transcript, then checked the repository to confirm the verticals he names.

What those sources show:
- **Definition.** The build chat's summary calls Venuvoy "a bilingual sports-trip planner, Hebrew first". The README says it "plans sports trips around real fixtures". It builds 2 or 3 alternative priced plans, shows a source and check date for every item, and tracks changes after unlock.
- **It does not sell.** The legal text says Venuvoy "does not sell tickets, flights or hotels".
- **Beyond football.** The wizard has 16 spectator sports plus hikes and runs. The shipped catalogs hold rows for 13 sports across 46 region files.
- **Sports activities.** "Active days" cover hikes, city runs and parkrun. "Sport nearby" covers places to play, from padel and climbing to shooting and skydiving, with data files for 521 cities.
- **Casinos.** They exist, but only as an opt-in, adults-only "Nightlife and casinos" evening visit with practical facts. No betting content and no partner links; the code records this as a founder decision.
- **Money.** One-time per-trip unlock, tracking and bundle prices, plus disclosed partner links.
- **Look.** The "Members' Club" design the founder chose: cream, racing green and brass, serif display type, a "V" crest.
- **Languages.** Hebrew by default and English; Russian, Arabic, French and Spanish are preview locales on a work branch.
- **Markets.** In the ads chat the founder asked for an international, English-first, community-first start.

# Venuvoy fact sheet for the ad team

LIVE means in the interface on the main branch (a927bc3, 11 Nov 2026); the public site was not checked, so demo or full mode is UNCLEAR. Paths are under /home/user/venuvoy.

## What Venuvoy is

Venuvoy is a sports-trip planner: a web app, Hebrew by default and English at /en. You say where and when you travel, which sports and clubs you love and what you can spend. It builds two or three different, priced, day-by-day plans around real published fixtures, with a source, a check date and a status on every item. A paid option then tracks the fixtures and alerts you to changes. It sells only its own planning and tracking. Its words: "Venuvoy plans sports trips around real fixtures." / "Venuvoy מתכננת טיולי ספורט סביב משחקים אמיתיים." (README.md:3-12); hero "A sports trip you can trust." / "טיול ספורט שאפשר לסמוך עליו." (src/features/landing/text.ts:11, 91).

For a twelve-year-old: tell Venuvoy where you are going and which sports you like, and it draws up a few trip plans around real games.

## What it covers

Catalog (src/data/regions/*.json): 11,711 events, 13 sports with events, 88 competitions, 705 teams, 786 venues, 56 countries, 46 regions. Only England is "Full coverage"; 17 regions are partial and 28 are "Marquee events only".

| Vertical | What the user gets | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Football | 5,834 events, about 40 competitions, 40 countries | LIVE |
| US and European leagues | MLB 2,428; NBA, EuroLeague, EuroCup 1,669; NHL and Slovak hockey 1,373; NFL 193 | LIVE |
| Motorsport, rugby, tennis, golf to watch | 104 (F1, MotoGP, Formula E, IndyCar, WEC); 44; 37; 20 | LIVE |
| Thin or empty sports | horse racing 5, athletics 2, cricket 1, cycling 1; boxing, darts, snooker are planner tiles with 0 events | PARTIAL |
| Casinos | "Nightlife and casinos" / "חיי לילה וקזינו" switch; 18 casinos in 17 cities; at most one per trip, on a free evening. Sports bars: PLANNED, 0 places | LIVE, opt-in, adults only |
| Active days | 51 hikes, 13 city runs, 110 parkruns in 10 regions, placed by the planner. Rides, ski days: PLANNED | LIVE |
| Sport nearby | 15,961 places in 520 cities: 13,975 to play, 152 tours and museums, 1,834 shops; includes 30 shooting ranges, 41 ziplines, 25 indoor skydiving | LIVE, added by hand |
| Golf rounds, stadium tours | 19 rounds, 11 indoor golf, 17 tours placed by the planner, England only | PARTIAL |
| Tickets | "Get tickets" guide per game, official seller first; 44 ticket sites listed; seat maps for 45 venues; Scam Shield link check | LIVE; live prices UNCLEAR |
| Hotels, car hire, tours, flights | search links to Booking.com and GetYourGuide. Flights: only the user's own landing and departure times, no search | LIVE as links; flights PARTIAL |

Evidence: src/features/wizard/types.ts:16-33; src/engine/casino.ts:1-48; src/data/regions/active/*.json; public/data/spots/v1/index.json; src/engine/spots.ts:116-117, 183-184.

## What a user does, step by step

1. Starts from the home form (country or city, dates, sport chips; button "See what's on" / "מה יש בתאריכים שלי"), from one typed sentence in Hebrew or English ("Tell us in one sentence" / "ספרו לנו במשפט אחד"), or from "Build a trip around this match".
2. The sentence only fills the planner: "Fill in the planner" / "מלאו לי את האשף" (src/features/intake/text.ts:5-14, 49-60). Casinos, hikes and runs are switches there.
3. Presses "Create plans" / "ליצור מסלולים" and gets two or three versions: "Big Matches", "Balanced", "Easy Pace".
4. Opens the trip page: Plan, Tickets, Prepare, On the trip (תוכנית · כרטיסים · הכנות · בדרך).
5. Adds "Sport nearby" / "ספורט בסביבה" places and own items by hand.
6. Buys tickets, flights and the hotel elsewhere, through the links; may pay for tracking alerts.

## What it does not do

- "It does not sell tickets, flights or hotels and is not a party to any purchase you make elsewhere." (src/features/legal/content.ts:67). Nothing is booked inside Venuvoy.
- No flight search or price. The budget is "Excluding flights and hotels" / "בלי טיסות ולינה" (src/features/wizard/text.ts:207, 555-556).
- Casinos: "Listed only as a place to visit. Venuvoy does not offer or promote gambling." / "מוצג כמקום לבקר בו בלבד. Venuvoy לא מציעה ולא מקדמת הימורים." (src/features/plan/text.ts:337, 818-819). Never with children, no betting content, no partner link. The sentence box does not understand "casino".
- No food, sightseeing or concerts, except items the user adds. No promise that tickets are available, no "where to watch", no adverts, and no "not affiliated with clubs" sentence. Legal pages are drafts.
- The planner is fixed code, not AI; a model only helps read a hard sentence, in the full version.

## Honest verbs

Plan, build, find, see what's on, compare, check, track, alert, "get tickets" (a guide to the official seller). Not honest for Venuvoy itself: book, buy, sell, reserve, "AI plans your trip", "anywhere in the world".

## Money

"Planning is free. Pay once per trip to edit, execute and watch it." / "התכנון חינם. משלמים פעם אחת לטיול כדי לערוך, לבצע ולעקוב." No subscription. Plan unlock ₪49, $15, €14 or £12; Tracking ₪99, $29, €27 or £23; Bundle ₪129, $39, €36 or £31 (src/features/pricing/priceBook.ts:25-29). Some partner links may pay commission; the order never depends on it. Whether real payment is switched on is UNCLEAR.

## Who it is for and how the founder talks about it

His product-defining messages in the build chat could not be reached. From the ads chat: "אנחנו מעבר לרק כדורגל, אנחנו טיולי ספורט באופן כללי, קזינואים, פעילויות ספורט, וכל כך הרבה יותר"; "אני רוצה להתחיל עם קהל בינלאומי קודם, שהכל יהיה באנגלית בינתיים"; "מה שמשנה זה הקהילה"; Timo and Luna should be "בין לאומי הומוריסטי ונחמד, מדבר בגובה העיניים". Code records the casino rule as a "founder decision": places to visit, practical facts only (src/engine/casino.ts:2-3).

"Members' Club" direction (src/styles/globals.css:5-10, 79-101): cream #f4eee1, ink #26221c, ivory card #fbf8f1, racing green #1e4d38, header band #16392b, brass #b8955a (#c9a96a on green), oxblood #6f1d29. ## What is new compared with "a football trip from one sentence"

- Sixteen sports in the planner, thirteen with events; football is half.
- Things travellers do themselves: hikes, runs, parkrun, golf rounds, about 16,000 places to play.
- An adults-only casino evening, as a place to visit; stadium tours, sports museums, club stores.
- Two or three plans instead of one, with sources, check dates and change alerts.

The intake works completely without it."; lines 19-27: it extracts "names and numbers only" and "never computes calendar dates, never returns a slug, a fixture or a price"; lines 32-38: called only in full mode and only when the local parse leaves words unplaced; "A fully understood sentence never leaves the device." Client gate: src/features/intake/IntakeBox.tsx:57-68 and src/features/intake/assist.ts:1-6.
